title: Sharing your work
summary: Push a branch to origin, then pull a teammate's commit.

say.never: Your project folder is the **local** copy. Teams also keep a shared copy on a server, like **GitHub**, called the **remote**. The remote is usually named **origin**. You work locally, then **push** to send your commits up, and **pull** to bring teammates' commits down. In this lesson `origin` is a private copy on this computer, so no account is needed.
say.bit: Local = your copy. Remote (`origin`) = the shared copy on GitHub. Push uploads, pull downloads. Here `origin` is a hidden local copy.

say.never: Open the **terminal**: hold **Ctrl** and tap the backtick key (above **Tab**).
say.bit: Open the terminal with Ctrl+` (above Tab).

waitFor.hint: press Ctrl and the backtick key (above Tab).

say.never: Type `cd 06-push` and press **Enter**. Then type `git push origin issue-18-team-colors` and press **Enter**. That sends your branch to `origin`. (Or use the **Publish Branch** button in the bottom-left corner.)
say.bit: `cd 06-push`, then `git push origin issue-18-team-colors` (or the Publish Branch button).

say.never: Now the other direction. Type `cd ../07-pull` and press **Enter**. A teammate added a commit to `develop` on `origin`. You're already on `develop`, so type `git pull` and press **Enter**. Open `Schedule.txt` to see the new line.
say.bit: `cd ../07-pull`, then `git pull` on `develop`. `Schedule.txt` gets your teammate's line.

marks.label: download and merge the new commits
